sections.h2: Register of Deeds address and phone
sections.html:
The office is at 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311, and the phone number is 423-728-7240. Land is recorded county by county here, so any deed for a house in Bradley County goes to this single office, no matter if the house is in Cleveland, in Charleston or out in the unincorporated hills between them.

Phone ahead if you are bringing a deed in person, and ask for the total recording charge for your page count and for the office's hours that day.

Bradley County's July 2025 estimate is 115,465 residents and 47,861 housing units. Owners live in 67.3 percent of the homes. The median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $261,900 and median gross rent is $1,030, a number landlords can use to compare selling with holding. Cleveland is the county seat and largest city, and Charleston is the other city. Public schools are split between Bradley County Schools and Cleveland City Schools.

Ridges run through the county, and Candies Creek Ridge crosses Cleveland. A lot on a slope needs a careful survey and drainage check before a buyer's lender signs off.

Sellers here should confirm which school system serves the address, since Bradley County Schools and Cleveland City Schools each draw their own buyers, and keep the parcel number handy. It appears on the tax bill and goes on the deed.

TitleSearcher is the vendor site the county recommends, and it offers online access to land records twenty-four hours a day. It holds images and index data for deeds, mortgages, releases, powers of attorney, restrictions, plat maps and other filings at the register's office.

The register's page also links a property fraud alert sign-up. Alerts watch for new filings under your name, which helps if you own a rental, inherited land or a vacant lot you seldom visit. A forger working against an empty house is counting on the owner not noticing.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed for your parcel and check three things: the spelling of every owner name, the legal description, and any deed of trust that was never released. A lender that was paid off but never filed a release leaves a cloud on the title, and a closing agent will ask you to clear it.

sections.h2: Taxes due when a deed is recorded
sections.html:
These taxes come from state law and do not vary by county. Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 as a realty transfer tax and $0.115 per $100 of debt as a mortgage tax, leaving the first $2,000 of debt untaxed.

Tax or ruleHow it works
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of the greater of price or value
Who pays itThe grantee (buyer) named on the deed
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exempt, paid by the borrower
Required statement on debt instrumentsMaximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes
Register receipt feeUp to $1 per receipt for each tax
Penalty for unpaid indebtedness tax$250 or double the unpaid tax, whichever is greater

Ask the title agent for the exact charge on your deal before closing.

A short list of transfers is excluded by the state manual. Many of them arise in estates, divorces and family moves, when an owner may want to sell in a hurry.

  • Deeds an executor signs to carry out a devise in a will.
  • Domestic settlement decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing parties.
  • A conveyance from one spouse to the other that creates or dissolves a tenancy by the entirety.
  • Transfers into a revocable living trust by the person who made it, and transfers back to that person or the spouse.
  • Real estate formerly held by tenants in common, and the release of a life estate to the remainder beneficiaries.
  • Transfers to or from a government entity.

An exempt transfer needs no oath of consideration. With a taxable deed, the buyer swears to the price or value on the deed's face while the register watches, and the state may later set that number beside the assessor's value.

Between unrelated parties, the price actually paid is normally what you state. When value is what sets the tax, the state treats the assessor's tax base, or an appraisal the assessor has accepted, as fair market value. Report less and you may face an audit, penalties and interest.

The Bradley County Assessor of Property is at the Courthouse Annex, 155 Broad Street NW, Room 105, phone 423-728-7125. It also operates a Tennessee property viewer with parcel data and tax maps. Before signing a deed with a stated value far from the assessor's figure for your house, look that figure up.

sections.h2: State rules that affect your deed
sections.html:
Several Department of Revenue rules are applied at the register's counter, and a closing that knows them in advance will not stall over a technicality.

  • Several deeds for the same tract in a single transfer are taxed once, and nothing is due until title passes by deed.
  • A modified or amended deed or deed of trust needs the earlier document's book and page, which shows the register that tax was already paid.
  • Any instrument showing debt must state the maximum principal indebtedness. The register cannot record it until the statement is given and the tax is paid.
  • When a buyer assumes a loan and the seller remains liable, no new debt exists and no mortgage tax is due. A new contract that releases the seller does create new debt, and it is taxed.
  • To prove tax was paid elsewhere, name the jurisdiction and give the book and page of the recorded document.

With a loan payoff, ask the lender how and when it will file the release of its deed of trust. That release clears the record, and the buyer's title agent will look for it.

sections.h2: Selling a Bradley County house for cash
sections.html:
Recording stays simple with a cash sale. We buy Bradley County houses as-is, and the deed is filed here like any other. Without a lender there is no deed of trust and no mortgage tax, though the buyer still pays the transfer tax and swears to the value. You choose the closing date, and nothing waits on loan approval.

Have the previous deed, your tax bill and any payoff figures on hand. If a deed contains an error, remember that the register records documents exactly as presented. The title company or attorney who drafted it can tell you how to fix it, and 423-728-7240 will confirm what the office needs to accept the corrected version.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Bradley County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311, phone 423-728-7240.

faqs.q: Can I search Bradley County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. TitleSearcher, the vendor the county points to, has land record images and index data all day and night, and the register's page links a property fraud alert sign-up.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Bradley County?
faqs.a: It is $0.37 per $100 of price or value, and every Tennessee county charges the same. The buyer on the deed owes it, collected by the register at recording.

faqs.q: Do I pay mortgage tax if I sell for cash?
faqs.a: No. Mortgage tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt past the first $2,000 and applies to instruments like a deed of trust, and a cash purchase has none.

faqs.q: Does the register fix errors in my deed?
faqs.a: The register records what is presented. Ask whoever drafted the deed how to correct it, then call 423-728-7240 to learn what the office needs.
